extraction.name: MINT-1T
extraction.description: MINT-1T is an open-source multimodal interleaved dataset comprising one trillion text tokens and 3.4 billion images across 1054 million documents. It scales existing open-source interleaved datasets by 10x and incorporates diverse sources including HTML documents, CommonCrawl PDFs, and ArXiv papers.
extraction.creator: Anas Awadalla, Le Xue, Oscar Lo, Manli Shu, Hannah Lee, Etash Guha, Matt Jordan, Sheng Shen, Mohamed Awadalla, Silvio Savarese, Caiming Xiong, Ran Xu, Yejin Choi, Ludwig Schmidt
extraction.citeAs: Awadalla, A., Xue, L., Lo, O., Shu, M., Lee, H., Guha, E., Jordan, M., Shen, S., Awadalla, M., Savarese, S., Xiong, C., Xu, R., Choi, Y., & Schmidt, L. (2024). MINT-1T: Scaling Open-Source Multimodal Data by 10x: A Multimodal Dataset with One Trillion Tokens. arXiv preprint arXiv:2406.11271v5.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was extracted from three primary sources: (1) HTML documents parsed from CommonCrawl WARC files (May 2017 to April 2024) by parsing each entry's DOM tree and filtering documents; (2) PDF documents extracted from CommonCrawl WAT files (February 2023 to April 2024 dumps), downloaded, and parsed using PyMuPDF to extract text reading order and anchor images; (3) ArXiv papers collected from ArXiv S3 buckets using TexSoup on LaTeX source files to interleave figure tags with text and strip preamble, bibs, and tables.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: None. However, the dataset relies on downloading external image URLs, and link rot may cause missing images over time. Also, non-retrievable image links were discarded during collection.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: CommonCrawl WARC files (May 2017 to April 2024), CommonCrawl WAT files (February 2023 to April 2024), and ArXiv LaTeX source files directly from ArXiv S3 buckets.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Text quality filtering: eliminated non-English text using FastText language identification (confidence threshold 0.65), removed NSFW URLs, applied RefinedWeb/MassiveText heuristic rules, and deduplicated 13-gram paragraphs using Dolma's Bloom filter (discarding documents with >80% duplicate paragraphs) and removed boilerplate text using CCNet's 2% snapshot exact deduplication. Image filtering: discarded broken links, filtered out images smaller than 150 pixels or larger than 20,000 pixels, filtered aspect ratios >2 for HTML and >3 for PDFs, deduplicated repeated images appearing >10 times per snapshot via SHA256 hashes, and deduplicated intra-document duplicate images. Safety filtering: ran an NSFW image detector and discarded documents with any NSFW image; masked PII by replacing email addresses and IP addresses.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: FastText language identification, Gant Laborde deep NN for NSFW detection, PyMuPDF, TexSoup, BFF (Bloom Filter), DataTrove
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors will actively maintain and update the dataset, responding to issues via GitHub/HuggingFace Issues tab and email. Updates and errata will be communicated via the HuggingFace README. Older versions are accessible via Git history. Contributions are accepted via HuggingFace Pull Requests. A Google Form is provided for individuals to request opt-out and sample removal.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Since data is sourced from the public web, it may include images of individuals and text about specific individuals, as well as sensitive personal information. Email addresses and IP addresses have been anonymized/masked.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Aims to democratize research and bridge the gap between open-source and proprietary multimodal foundation models. Risks include exposure to web-scraped sensitive or offensive content.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: To avoid demographic bias often introduced by model-based quality filtering, rules-based heuristics were used instead of text quality classifiers. The PDF subset is biased towards Science and Technology due to the nature of academic PDFs, and the dataset is restricted to English text.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: PDF parsing using PyMuPDF has limitations: images are sometimes undetected, and arbitrary document layouts can result in incorrect reading order across columns. External image links may suffer from link rot.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Pre-training large multimodal models (LMMs) capable of processing interleaved image and text sequences, generative multimodal modelling, and multimodal document retrieval. Non-recommended uses: military applications, and training models to ingest or generate personally identifying information (such as facial recognition or sensitive personal content).
